title: Why does planning a trip still feel like a full-time job?
text: Medium Why does planning a trip still feel like a full-time job? | by Fonda Irena | Sep, 2026 | Medium Sitemap Open in app Sign up Sign in Medium Logo Get app Write Search Sign up Sign in Fonda Irena More about me: https://fonda-santoso-website.netlify.app/ Member-only story Travel App Vibe Coding Product Management Ai Product Management Why does planning a trip still feel like a full-time job? Fonda Irena 3 min read · Sep 21, 2026 -- Listen Share A trip is supposed to be something you look forward to. Instead, planning one can mean opening Google Maps, searching through blogs, saving Instagram posts, comparing hotels, checking flight times, copying restaurant names into Notes, sending links to friends, and somehow ending up with 14 browser tabs and no actual itinerary. I realized I had a strange relationship with travel planning. I loved the idea of the trip, yet I hated planning the trip. And that made me wonder: What if travel planning didn’t feel like research? What if it felt like the beginning of the trip itself? That question became the starting point for Kumo. Press enter or click to view image in full size Most travel apps stop when the trip begins Think about most travel products. Before your trip, you’re searching, saving, comparing and planning. Then the trip starts. You use a completely different set of tools. Your camera roll fills up with photos. You send messages to friends.
